Application Fee
How much is the application fee?
For U.S. students, the degree and certificate application fee is $65, and the nondegree application fee is $30.
For international students, the application fee is $85.
Veterans and military service members receive a discounted rate of $40 on their degree or certificate application fee. This represents more than a 35 percent decrease from the standard application fee.
What methods of payment are accepted?
The Fox Graduate School accepts Visa, Mastercard, Discover Card, American Express, checks, and money orders. Checks or money orders must be payable to “The Pennsylvania State University” in U.S. dollars, and must be drawn from a U.S. bank.
A debit card may be used only if it is processed as a credit card payment (without the PIN). Credit card gift cards are also acceptable.
Can someone pay the application fee on my behalf?
Yes, you, another individual, or a company or organization may pay the application fee by credit card via the Fox Graduate School Payment Portal, or by check/money order using the Application Fee Form.
Can the application fee be paid after my application is submitted?
Yes, you or another individual may pay the application fee by credit card via the Fox Graduate School Payment Portal, or by check/money order using the Application Fee Form. After this payment is made, your application will be reviewed.
Can the application fee be waived?
In certain situations, an applicant may be granted a fee waiver. If this is the case, you will be given instructions by your graduate program or another Penn State office for how to complete this as part of the application.
If I'm applying for a degree and certificate program, do I need to pay a fee for both?
Yes, you will need pay the fee for each graduate program application you submit.
IMPORTANT: You may only apply to one degree program at a time. If you submit additional degree applications, only your most recently submitted degree application will be reviewed.
Is the application fee refundable?
No, application fees are nonrefundable.
When is my fee processed?
Fees are processed as soon as the payment is received.
IMPORTANT: The application fee is processed immediately; however, your application status may not be available during the first 24 hours.
Why does my credit card statement show multiple application fee transactions?
This may happen if you hit the credit card payment button more than once while waiting for the fee payment to be processed. Check your credit card statement for duplicate payments. Typically, one transaction is only a hold and will resolve within seven to ten business days. If both transactions still appear on your account, please contact info@foxgradschool.psu.edu.
Application Status
How will I know if my application is complete?
When your application is submitted, you will get a confirmation email. You may also log in to the application and check your status page for confirmation, or contact your intended graduate program.
How will I know if my mailed application documents have been received?
Check the Status page of your Fox Graduate School Application to see which documents have been received and which have been reviewed.
When is my application reviewed?
Each graduate program has its own application review process, deadlines, and timeframe. Please check your intended program’s website for more information.
When will I know if I am admitted?
You will receive an email when a decision has been made about your application. If you do not hear back, please contact your intended graduate program, as each plan has its own admission deadlines and processes. You can find contact information by searching for your program on the Graduate Bulletin.
Where do I check the status of my application?
On the Status page of your application. If you do not see the status there, you should contact your intended graduate program. You can find contact information by searching for your program on the Graduate Bulletin.
Applying for Admission
Can I be accepted conditionally if I have not yet taken English proficiency tests?
No. If required, English proficiency scores (TOEFL or IELTS) must be submitted prior to being offered admission. Please note that specific graduate programs may require all international applicants to submit a TOEFL or IELTS score, regardless of their academic background and country of origin, and may have more stringent requirements.
View Minimum Acceptable Test Scores
Do all my materials need to be received by the deadline?
Graduate programs set and enforce deadlines. Please check with your intended graduate program. You can find contact information by searching for your program on the Graduate Bulletin.
International applicants must submit materials at least four months prior to the semester they plan to enroll; however, the application deadline for some graduate programs is much earlier than this. All applicants should consult their intended graduate programs for specific requirements.
How do I apply as a transfer student?
All students, including transfer students, have the same requirements for admission. They are required to submit Penn State’s Fox Graduate School application, pay the application fee, and submit official copies of their academic transcripts.
If you are currently enrolled as doctoral student at another institution, please be aware that you will need to meet Penn State’s doctoral degree requirements, even if you already met some of these at your current institution.
These requirements include:
residency
passing of a qualifying, comprehensive, and final oral examination
writing a satisfactory dissertation that is approved by both the doctoral committee and the Fox Graduate School
How do I change my contact information after an application has been submitted?
Visit Penn State Account Management. Once updated on the Account Management site, your information will later shortly after in the Fox Graduate School application system.
How do I change other information after an application has been submitted?
Email your updates to admissions@foxgradschool.psu.edu. The revised information or documents will be added to your application and will not replace what you have already submitted. Please note any changes to an application after it is submitted will not be visible to the applicant. You will not see the updated information/document.
How do I reapply to a program I previously applied to but was denied admission?
You will need to complete a new graduate online application, pay the required application fee, and provide the required program documents. If you are reapplying to the same program, please contact your intended graduate program to determine if updated documents are necessary. You can find contact information by searching for your program on the Graduate Bulletin.
Where can I view Penn State’s academic calendar?
You can find the Penn State's academic calendar on the University Registrar’s website.
Who makes the admission or denial decision?
Your intended graduate program will recommend your acceptance to the Fox Graduate School. After final review by the Fox Graduate School, you will receive formal notification of your admission. Questions concerning your admission or denial should be directed to your intended graduate program. You can find contact information by searching for your program on the Graduate Bulletin.
Will I be contacted if there are questions about my application?
Yes, you may be contacted by either your intended graduate program or the Fox Graduate School. Each graduate program has its own procedures for evaluating applications, and the Fox Graduate School ensures that all applicants meet Penn State’s minimum requirements for all graduate programs.
Reference Questions
How can someone send a physical letter of reference to the graduate program?
Please contact your intended program of study for information on whether reference letters can be sent directly to the program.
How and when are my referees notified to submit a letter of reference?
If the intended graduate program has elected to use the online reference features, your referees will be notified via email upon submission of your graduate application.
If the intended graduate program does not to use the online reference features, you will need to contact your references.
You can find contact information by searching for your program on the Graduate Bulletin.
Does my graduate program have a specific letter of reference format I need to follow?
Please refer to your intended graduate program website for more information on reference requirements. You can find contact information by searching for your program on the Graduate Bulletin.
Test Scores
Will Penn State accept TOEFL score reports from another school?
No. TOEFL scores must come directly from Educational Testing Service (ETS).
Why aren't my test scores showing on my application?
Official test scores do not appear on unsubmitted applications. After you request that test scores be sent to Penn State, it can take up to twenty business days for them to appear in your submitted application. If you do not see test scores after ten business days, contact us for help at testscores@foxgradschool.psu.edu.
Where should I have my test scores sent?
GRE and TOEFL: Use school code 2660 to send scores to Penn State.
IELTS: Select "Penn State University, University Park – Graduate School"
MAT: Select "Penn State University" or use school code 2609.
GMAT: Select “Penn State University- University Park,” and, if prompted, select your graduate program and graduate program location.
What if I plan on taking my test after submitting my application?
Leave the test scores section blank and enter a statement in the comment section of the application stating which test you will be taking and when you plan to take it.
I incorrectly reported my test results on the application. How do I correct them?
Please contact your intended graduate program with this information. You can find contact information by searching for your program on the Graduate Bulletin.
Official scores must be sent directly to Penn State from the appropriate reporting agency (ETS, Pearson Vue, etc.).
I have questions about test scores. Who do I ask?
All questions regarding test scores should be directed to your intended graduate program. You can find contact information by searching for your program on the Graduate Bulletin.
How long does it take for my test scores to be received by the Fox Graduate School?
This varies depending on the test type (GRE, TOEFL, etc.). Please refer to the testing agency’s website to find out when your scores will be or were reported. It may take up to twenty business days for your scores to be received at Penn State.
How do I know if my test scores have been received?
Check the status page of your application to confirm whether test scores are received.
Do I need to take the TOEFL or IELTS?
The language of instruction at Penn State is English. All international applicants must take and submit scores for the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) iBT or the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) Academic Test, with the exceptions noted on the preparing to apply page.
Do I need to take the GRE?
All questions regarding the GRE should be directed to your intended graduate program. You can find contact information by searching for your program on the Graduate Bulletin.
Transcripts and Records
What are official and unofficial transcripts?
An official transcript must meet three criteria:
It is received from the applicant in an envelope sealed by the issuing institution, or comes directly from the issuing institution via postal mail, electronic mail, or a trusted third party vendor.
It bears the institutional seal.
It bears the official signature of the institution’s registrar (or recorder of records).
An unofficial transcript is a copy of an official transcript. Examples of documents that are not acceptable as an official transcript include:
Advising transcripts
Degree audit from a self-service website
A copy of a transcript(s) that is prepared and signed by a faculty member, city or government official, or notary public
If I have international credentials, what do you consider as "official" documents?
Your international records will be considered complete and official if:
each document is an original or an attested copy that is certified by the issuing institution;
it is a comprehensive record of all study completed, in the form of a transcript or yearly marksheets;
it includes all degree certificates conferred;
each document is submitted with an officially certified English translation.
The University reserves the right to request official credentials or additional supporting documentation at any time during the admission process as deemed necessary.
How do I know if my transcripts have been received?
You can check your status of your application, including receipt of references, documents and test scores, by logging into your existing account in the Fox Graduate School application. Once there, you will find a hyperlink labeled “status” that will allow you access this information.
Do I need to upload transcripts/records from all institutions I have attended?
Yes, if you are applying to a degree program, you are required to upload copies of official transcripts/records/degree certificates from all institutions attended. All transcripts and academic records uploaded to the application are then considered “unofficial” and will be used for application purposes only.

With a diverse range of graduate programs spanning various disciplines, Penn State offers students the opportunity to pursue advanced studies in fields at the forefront of innovation and discovery. The university's commitment to research is evident through its state-of-the-art facilities and collaborative research initiatives, providing students with invaluable hands-on experience and opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration.”
